stories.title: Govt and unions to prepare for formal talks on pay
stories.summary: Government and trade unions will prepare for the start of formal negotiations on a new public sector pay deal at the Workplace Relations Commission tomorrow. It follows an announcement last night that both sides had agreed to enter into official discussions after a period of sustained deadlock, including Wednesday's national strike involving over 300,000 public sector workers. A second 24-hour strike by public sector workers for next Wednesday was suspended on Friday. Last night's announcement came after meetings throughout Saturday aimed at exploring whether the formal process could begin, with a resolution not initially expected after a single day of engagement. Independent Chair Kevin Foley met a trade union representative, ICTU General Secretary Owen Reidy, and a Government representative, Oonagh Buckley, who is Secretary General of the Department of the Environment, at the offices of the Forsa trade union in Dublin. Shortly before 9pm, the trio confirmed an agreement had been reached for formal pay talks to start on Monday.

stories.title: Talks on public sector pay deal to begin at WRC on Monday
stories.summary: Formal talks aimed at agreeing a new public sector pay deal will begin at the Workplace Relations Commission (WRC) on Monday. It follows meetings throughout the day aimed at exploring whether the formal process could begin after a second 24-hour strike by public sector workers for next Wednesday was suspended yesterday. Independent Chair Kevin Foley today met a trade union representative, ICTU General Secretary Owen Reidy, and a Government representative, Oonagh Buckley, who is Secretary General of the Department of the Environment. Shortly before 9pm, they confirmed agreement had been reached for formal pay talks to start on Monday. In a statement, they said: "Following engagement with the parties, we believe that discussions at the WRC should get under way on Monday 19 October. The discussions should commence with pay related matters, including the trade unions' claims on cost-of-living effects between 2021–2025, this year, and for the duration of any agreement". "There is a need to rebuild trust and confidence in industrial relations in the public sector by addressing commitments made in the context of the previous agreement," they added.

stories.title: Four candidates to contest Seanad bye-election seat
stories.summary: Four candidates are to contest the forthcoming Seanad bye-election for the remaining vacancy in the Oireachtas. The vote to fill a seat on the Seanad's Cultural and Educational panel was triggered by the success of Fine Gael's Sean Kyne in the Galway West Dáil bye-election in May. The Seanad returning officer ruled on nominations yesterday with ballot papers to be issued to those voting on Friday 23 October. The poll closes on Friday 6 November. There are 233 members of the Dáil and Seanad who are eligible to vote, of which 51.5% are representatives of Fianna Fáil and Fine Gael. Former Dublin city lord mayor Ray McAdam has been selected as the Fine Gael candidate, having ran unsuccessfully in the Dublin Central bye-election in May to fill the seat of his party colleague Pascal Donohoe, receiving 10.67% of the vote. Success for the Dublin City Councillor would be regarded as strategically important for Fine Gael, with the party currently without Oireachtas representation in Mr McAdam's Dáil constituency of Dublin Central and the neighbouring constituency of Dublin North West.

stories.title: What you need to know ahead of the 31 Oct tax deadline
stories.summary: If you need to complete a self-assessed tax return, then 31 October is one of the most important dates in the year. It's the standard annual Pay and File deadline managed by the Revenue Commissioners. The document to file an income tax return in Ireland is a Form 11. It’s used by non-PAYE workers and PAYE workers with additional income who are responsible for evaluating how much tax they owe. The tax is calculated on earnings for the previous year, so filing on 31 October will be for earnings in 2025. "Check and make sure you’re claiming all that you’re entitled to," advised Cróna Clohisey, Director of Members and Advocacy in Chartered Accountants Ireland.

stories.title: Russian claims of Ukraine territory advance 'an illusion'
stories.summary: Ukraine has rejected Russia's claim to have captured more than 1,800sq/km of territory and nearly 100 ⁠settlements, including the eastern town of Dobropillia, since 1 September. Yesterday, the chief of Russia's General Staff, Valery Gerasimov, told President Vladimir Putin that Russian forces had captured 92 Ukrainian settlements and made significant territorial gains since the start of last month. Ukraine's General Staff spokesman Andriy Kovaliov dismissed the claims as false. "In fact, through their active operations, the Ukrainian Defence Forces have liberated more territory ‌since the beginning of autumn ⁠than the enemy has managed to capture," he said in an emailed statement. "The Russian military leadership continues to create an illusion of major victories for its political leadership and domestic audience," he said. Russia's advances along the front line have slowed this year but ‌its forces have been bearing down on the so-called "fortress belt" cities of Sloviansk and Kramatorsk, the capture ⁠of which would bring Russia closer to its goal of seizing ‌the entire industrialised Donetsk region.

stories.title: Let the Gods smile upon them - clubs chase elusive titles
stories.summary: "To win just once against the odds and once be smiled on by the Gods." It's hard not to think back to Mayo's shock All-Ireland win over Kerry in July and hear the crowd bellowing out the Saw Doctors hit 'To Win Just Once.' That lap of honour, with the lyrics reverberating around Croke Park at full volume, was not only one of the Irish sporting moments of the year, but one of the most memorable of all time. Truagh Gaels know what it's like to race around Croke Park with a cup having done so back in 2014 following an All-Ireland IFC final win over Mayo outfit Kiltane who had a young Tommy 'Goals' Conroy in the corner, not to be confused with his namesake who was part of that green and red wave that swept all before them this summer. Another 11 clubs have lifted the trophy after the Monaghan club, but converting that into senior success is no guarantee. Indeed, the evidence suggests that it's unlikely. Of those 11 sides, two have won senior titles since - Westport coming out on top in Mayo in 2022 and Rathmore winning the Kerry Club crown last month. Only two other clubs have even made it to a final with Cullyhanna losing out to Madden in last year's Armagh final.
stories.rssSummary: It's a jam-packed weekend of club final action as teams all over Ireland try to achieve their dreams. None more so than Truagh Gaels who are hoping to add their name to the Monaghan roll of honour.

stories.title: Mullen: 2026 was a year of 'soul searching' in Kilkenny
stories.summary: Kilkenny attacker Adrian Mullen acknowledges there was plenty of time for soul searching in the off-season after their shock early exit from the championship at the provincial stage in 2026. Mullen's Ballyhale Shamrocks side are back in the Kilkenny SHC decider once again with their fellow aristocrats in Tullaroan providing the opposition in a final which pits together two teams at the top of the roll of honour in the county. The final comes at the end of an unusually difficult year for Kilkenny hurling, in which they mustered just four wins from 11 competitive games and their reign in Leinster ended abruptly following losses in both Salthill and Parnell Park and a surprise draw in Tullamore. Derek Lyng's four-year stint in charge, which yielded three successive Leinster titles and an All-Ireland final appearance in 2023, ended shortly after the defeat to Dublin. "Naturally enough there's going to be a massive level of disappointment there because obviously you know that probably wasn't in the script," Mullen says of the Leinster exit. "You could see it after the game with Derek and even the players. I think that's fairly natural. There'd be something wrong if you didn't feel that level of disappointment.

stories.title: Nato brace sees ruthless Chelsea past Everton
stories.summary: Morgan Rogers' eventful afternoon at Everton could have ended with a sending-off before half-time but his good fortune was to Chelsea’s benefit as the England forward delivered the key moment in a 2-0 victory. The €137million summer signing was already on a yellow card for a tussle with James Tarkowski when he went in studs up in a 50-50 with James Garner, catching his opponent high up on his shin. It was a challenge neither referee Paul Tierney nor VAR felt warranted a second caution or even a straight red much to Everton’s frustration and that turned to annoyance when the 24-year-old’s driving run to the byline created the breakthrough for Pedro Neto 44 seconds after half-time. Rogers’ later tumbling in the penalty area after brushing up against Tarkowski only enhanced his role as villain in the eyes of home fans. When Neto slid home from Jordan Henderson’s deflected free-kick for the first Premier League double of his career, the end of Everton’s unbeaten start to the season was confirmed even with 11 minutes of added time still remaining. However, it was not all good news for the visitors as they had goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez carried off and taken to hospital after a clash of heads with Toffees centre-back Jarrad Branthwaite.

stories.title: Cullen: Carbery 'more mature' person on Leinster return
stories.summary: Leo Cullen believes Joey Carbery has come back to Leinster a "more mature person", as the out-half prepares to mark his return to his home province this afternoon. The out-half played 37 times for Leinster between 2016 and 2018 before joining Munster, where he endured an injury-hit six seasons, with the last two years spent at Bordeaux-Begles. The 30-year-old's final months at Bordeaux were hampered by an ACL injury, with Carbery now set to mark his return to action off the bench this afternoon. "He has been unlucky - we actually named him on the bench for the round two game [against Sharks] and he'd a minor tweak that week. "He's been great since he came back, it's great for Ollie [Coffey] to have that experience outside him. "We'll see how the game plays out, Joey gives us great versatility given he can slot in at No 15 as well if needed."

stories.title: Wexford Festival Opera - Croí na Féile celebrates 75 years of WFO
stories.summary: We proudly present a live presentation from this year's Wexford Festival Opera - join us for Croí na Féile, an all-star celebration of 75 years of WFO. This is Croí na Féile - Irish for the Heart of the Festival (pronounced kree nah fay-leh), a one-night-only concert bringing together four of the world's most acclaimed opera stars on one stage: Ermonela Jaho. Joseph Calleja, Daniela Barcellona and Giorgi Manoshvili. Together with the Wexford Festival Opera Orchestra, conducted by Daniele Callegari, they will perform music by Verdi, Puccini, Bizet, Massenet, Rossini and more. You'll hear our stars perform iconic arias from Tosca, Carmen, Atttila, Don Carlo, Rigoletto and La Traviata. Join us for a night to be remembered in the company of the biggest stars in opera. Find out more about this year's Wexford Festival Opera programme here

stories.title: Caitríona Balfe stars in Colm Tóibín's A Long Winter
stories.summary: The trailer for the Caitríona Balfe-starring A Long Winter has been released ahead of the acclaimed film's arrival in Irish cinemas next year. A Long Winter is the big-screen adaptation of the Colm Tóibín short story of the same name, with director Andrew Haigh (All of Us Strangers, 45 Years) behind the lens. Alongside Outlander star Balfe, the cast of A Long Winter also includes Fred Hechinger (Thelma, Gladiator II), Ebon Moss-Bachrach (The Bear, The Fantastic Four: First Steps), Kit Connor (Heartstopper, Warfare), D'Pharaoh Woon-A-Tai (Warfare, Reservation Dogs), and Martin Freeman (Sherlock, The Hobbit). The story is "set in the mountains as autumn draws to a close and a family prepares for the long winter ahead", and director Haigh has adapted Tóibín's short story for the screen. Filmed on location in Alberta, Canada, A Long Winter has already screened at the BFI London Film Festival, the Toronto International Film Festival, and the New York Film Festival. A Long Winter will open in Irish cinemas on 15 January, 2027.

stories.title: How Ireland Fashion Week created a homecoming for Irish designers
stories.summary: Sarah Magliocco looks back on Ireland Fashion Week 2026, speaking to the organisers, designers and creatives behind a showcase that brought the world stage to Irish design. Ireland Fashion Week has just closed its second year, and with a stacked schedule, impressive venues, international interest and scores of social media impressions, it's secured all the hallmarks that befit fellow fashion weeks across the world. However, the distinctly Irish elements have not been lost in that process, and nowhere was that more apparent than the theme of this year’s events. 'Coming Home: An Island In Motion’ made reference to Ireland’s global impact on the fashion industry, while influencing designers to reflect on the idea of coming home, a concept held so dearly by a diaspora that stretches to all corners of the earth. "But that's changed in the last few years, in particular where people are able to come home but also people don't necessarily have to leave, and we also have people from the rest of the world coming to Ireland and calling it home." A Galway native, McDonnell relocated to Paris to pursue her career in the luxury fashion industry while still in university. She was called home to create a platform where Irish design could be appreciated by a wider audience and Irish creatives would have paid opportunities to showcase their work.

stories.title: Trump paused Russia sanctions to 'analyse' impact - Rubio
stories.summary: US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that US President Donald Trump's waiver of sweeping sanctions and tariffs on Russia would be a 60-day pause to "analyse" their impact on the global economy. "The president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy and even to the US economy," Mr Rubio said, noting that the economic restrictions involved a number of countries, not just Russia. He said various conflicts were impacting global energy prices, including the US war on Iran and attacks on Saudi Arabia by Yemen's Houthis. "These conflicts around the world are starting to crash into each other, and they're having an impact not just on global oil and diesel prices" but on economies as well, Mr Rubio said. Mr Trump said his decision would benefit the US, though it was unclear if he had actually made up his mind on the matter. "We'll figure it out, and you'll figure it out," he said. "It's a very good decision, and it's going to be a decision that's good for the country, and I think good for the world."

stories.title: Unions suspend next week's planned strike action
stories.summary: Public sector unions have suspended next Wednesday's planned strike action following discussions with the Government. More than 300,000 public sector workers including nurses, doctors, teachers and civil servants, engaged in strike action last Wednesday over delays in agreeing a new public sector pay deal. In a statement earlier, the Public Services Committee of ICTU said that following discussions with Government representatives "over the last 24 hours, a meeting of the 19 unions affiliated to the ICTU PSC has agreed to suspend strike action due to take place next Wednesday". PSC Chair Kevin Callinan said that the Government agreed to appoint independent third party Kevin Foley, to carry out "an intensive and focused exercise aimed at constructing a basis for formal negotiations at the Workplace Relations Commission". Mr Callinan said that Mr Foley will be assisted by one trade union and one employer nominee, and that the process may get under way tomorrow morning. The Government confirmed this evening that Kevin Foley, Oonagh Buckley and Owen Reidy have been appointed to undertake a "focused and intensive exercise with the parties aimed at constructing a basis for formal negotiations at the Workplace Relations Commission".

stories.title: Uisce Éireann CEO defends €118,000 pay rise
stories.summary: Uisce Éireann CEO Niall Gleeson has defended a €118,000 increase in his overall salary to €391,953 - saying he and the utility are providing value for money to the public. Mr Gleeson was asked about the pay rise during the latest meeting of the Dáil Public Accounts Committee, amid separate questions over a €4,000 spend on PR advice before attending the meeting with TDs and senators. During a robust exchange, Sinn Féin TD Cathy Bennett told Mr Gleeson, "I have to say you must be doing an amazing job" because his salary has increased by €118,000, a rise first reported in July. Ms Bennett compared the rise to the far smaller increase being sought by public sector workers taking part in nationwide strikes, before asking: "How does someone receive that increase in one year?" The Sinn Féin TD said, "I don't know how you can sit here and condone it [the salary]", referencing problems some of her constituents in Co Monaghan have in terms of accessing clean water, water connections, and water that is not "brown". In response, Mr Gleeson said his pay rise was agreed after "an independent review of all salaries" at utilities, and that "the board [of Uisce Éireann] took the recommendations" and agreed to them.

stories.title: AIB cuts 4-year fixed rate for mortgages over €250,000
stories.summary: AIB has today announced a cut of up to 0.35% on its four-year fixed rate for mortgages over €250,000. AIB said the new rate, which is available immediately for new and existing customers, will benefit those whose homes do not have a Building Energy Rating of B3 or higher. The bank said that customers are increasingly opting for the certainty of a competitively priced fixed rate after the ECB increased rates by 0.25% twice this year. Almost nine in ten new AIB customers have opted for a fixed rate this year, it noted. AIB said a monthly repayment on its new €350,000 AIB High Value 4-year fixed rate mortgage, with a loan to value of 50 to 80% over a 25-year term, will be €1,695.30. The previous monthly repayment would have been €1,750.82, representing a saving of €55.52 a month, €666.24 a year, or €4,715.72 over the 25-year term of the mortgage.

stories.title: Pope holds phone call with Putin during hospital recovery
stories.summary: Pope Leo XIV has held a phone call with Russian President Vladimir Putin, the Vatican said, as the pope continues to recover in hospital after undergoing surgery for lung cancer. The Vatican said the pope is showing "steady improvement" following Tuesday's surgery. During the call with Mr Putin, the American pontiff expressed "deep concern" for the humanitarian situation in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky. Pope Leo urged Mr Putin for a truce to allow the entry of first aid and food supplies into the town, the Vatican said, and to permit a voluntary evacuation of the civilian population. The call with Mr Putin came after the Vatican said that the pope is now able to do normal daily activities with full autonomy. The pope will make his first public appearance since his hospitalisation on Sunday to deliver the traditional Angelus prayer, while preparations continue for his planned November trip to South America, the Vatican said.

stories.title: Glen raising the Barr as old rivals dig into storied past
stories.summary: Heading into the semi-finals of the Cork hurling championship, there was little talk of the old order being restored. Kanturk were the team of the championship heading into the penultimate stage, knocking out Blackrock and Sarsfields, and full of confidence they would inflict the same fate on traditional powerhouse St Finbarr's and reach a first-ever senior decider. On the other side, top seeds Midleton were fancied by many to see off a Glen Rovers side that only suffered an ignominious relegation from the senior ranks three years previous. Neither semi-final will go down as a classic, but when the dust settled, it was the Glen and the Barrs left standing and a first final meeting between the sides since 1988. Their first took place in 1934, the Glen winning the first of eight-in-a-row, with future Taoiseach and decorated Cork hurler Jack Lynch in their ranks. When that winning sequence came to an end, it was the Barrs that once again ruled the roost. In 1953, Lynch, by then a local TD, applied for a bridging loan of £10,000 (close to €500,000 in today's money) on behalf of the club to build Glen Hall. When asked what he proposed to put down as his collateral for such a sum of money, Lynch famously replied: "The people of Blackpool are my collateral." It was demolished in June 1998, a year before Lynch's death.

stories.title: Rabbitte eager to return for Athenry All-Ireland defence
stories.summary: Olwen Rabbitte began the year with an emotional All-Ireland club title with Athenry, and hopes to finish it back on the pitch to help in the defence of their crown. And much has happened in between. With father Joe, a three-time All-Ireland winner with the Athenry hurlers and a two-time All-Star himself, as manager and sister Sabina for company, Athenry dug in to see off St Finbarr's in the replayed final last January. The death of 20-year-old player Kate Moran in April 2022 from an injury in a senior league match against Ardrahan rocked the club, though she was never far from the thoughts of the players and management team. Speaking at the launch of the AIB Club Championships 2026/27, Rabbitte, who counted Moran as a close friend, said it was a "really emotional journey" for all concerned. When the team was presented with their All-Ireland medals, one was set aside for Moran, with her father present to accept it on her behalf. "It was an emotional thing to witness, but it was lovely that her spirit lives on."

stories.title: Fixtures confirmed for LOI play-off semi-finals
stories.summary: The dates and venues for the League of Ireland First Division play-off semi-finals have been confirmed. Longford Town and Kerry secured the final two spots on Friday evening, and have been rewarded with clashes against UCD and Bray Wanderers respectively. Strokestown Road will host the first leg of the Longford versus College game on Saturday 24 October at 7.30pm, with Mounthawk Park the venue for the first leg of Kerry and Bray at 7.45pm on the same night. The return legs will take place the following Tuesday, 27 October, with a kick off of 7.45pm at both the UCD Bowl and the Carlisle Grounds. stories.title: Hard to see past more French dominance in Champions Cup
stories.summary: For six seasons in a row, the Investec Champions Cup has been residing in France, and it's hard to see it leaving any time soon. Bordeaux-Begles, Toulouse and La Rochelle have shared those six titles evenly, with Leinster losing four of the finals, and if there is to be a challenger to the French rule, it once again looks like being Leo Cullen's side. For so long, this competition was a source of joy for Irish sides; Ulster were the first province to lift the trophy in 1999, before Munster picked up two in 2006 and 2008, and then Leinster's golden years where they won three titles in four years between 2009 and 2012, before adding another in 2018. Since then, the Champions Cup has been synonymous with both hope and heartbreak for Leinster, who have lost five finals since 2019. Meanwhile, the remaining provinces have been reduced to making up the numbers. Since the expansion of the tournament to 24 teams in the 2020/21 season, Munster have made two quarter-finals, while Ulster and Connacht haven't been beyond the Round of 16. Coming into this season, Toulouse and Bordeaux look on paper to be alone in the top tier, with Leinster, Bath, Northampton Saints and perhaps Montpellier just below. The hope for that quartet will be that the two French powerhouses end up on similar sides of the draw in the knockout stage, in order for at least one of them to fall along the way.

stories.title: Wexford Festival Opera - watch Rossini's L'equivoco stravagante
stories.summary: We proudly present a live presentation from this year's Wexford Festival Opera - L'equivoco stravagante by Gioachino Rossini, with a libretto by Gaetano Gasbarri. A joyous early work by Rossini, L'equivoco stravagante is a fast-paced, playful exploration of social climbing and the lengths we go to for love. Musically brilliant, it’s the ultimate fun night at the opera. A sparkling farce of absurd misunderstandings, youthful wit, rapid-fire ensemL'equivoco stravagantebles and comic excess, L’equivoco stravagante was Rossini’s first large-scale opera. It vanished from the repertoire after falling foul of the censor due to its subversive libretto. Wexford was one of the first companies to present it in 1968. The title means something like 'The Bizzare Misunderstanding' and premiered in Bologna in 1811, when the young composer was still only 19 years of age. This production returns following a historic public vote last summer. In a first for the Festival, audiences from 30 countries chose (by way of a vote) the 'fun’ opera for the 75th Anniversary, marking the first time a production has been selected by popular demand. Directed by Max Hoehn and conducted by Riccardo Bisatti, both making their Wexford debuts, this production is a masterclass in Rossini’s signature buffo (comic) style. In it we meet Gamberotto, a wealthy farmer with high-society ambitions for his bookish daughter, Ernestina. While he attempts to marry her off to the rich (but dim-witted) Buralicchio, the penniless Ermanno has other plans. What follows is a whirlwind of subversion, outrageous disguises, and a ‘bizarre misunderstanding’ involving a fake identity that once proved too scandalous for the 19th-century censors. stories.title: Bob Geldof reflects on Live Aid and Ireland's generosity
stories.summary: Singer, author and humanitarian Bob Geldof has said Live Aid offered a glimpse of the Ireland he had always believed existed, praising the generosity and kindness shown in response to the charity event. Live Aid took place on July 13, 1985, with simultaneous concerts at Wembley Stadium in London and John F Kennedy Stadium in Philadelphia. Organised by Geldof and musician Midge Ure, the event brought together music legends including Queen, U2, David Bowie, Elton John, Madonna and Paul McCartney to raise funds for famine relief in Ethiopia. Geldof was at Wembley Stadium as the concert was about to begin when the Irish production team contacted him. The women were waiting outside and wanted to hand them over. Concerned that they might later regret such a personal sacrifice, Geldof asked the organisers to ensure they were certain of their decision. He instructed them to hold the rings for a week, giving the women the opportunity to reclaim them if they changed their minds. Reflecting on Ireland's generosity, he said: "Pro rata, as we all know famously, this country did more than any other country in the world."

stories.title: Creative Director McGirr to leave McQueen after 3 years
stories.summary: Seán McGirr, the Dublin-born designer, is exiting storied fashion house McQueen after three years as the brand's Creative Director. Kering, the parent company of the London-based fashion house, made the annoucement today, just weeks after the brand's momentous return to the London Fashion Week circuit. McGirr joined McQueen in 2023, succeeding Sarah Burton, who took over as Creative Director in 2010 after the death of Lee Alexander McQueen and had a career spanning 26 years with the fashion house. That show now feels particularly significant, as McGirr invited jeweller and former McQueen collaborator, Shaun Leane, to create pieces for the runway for the first time in 16 years, fulfilling a long-held ambition of his. stories.summary: A "serious incident" at a military base in western Canada killed and injured multiple people and sparked a huge blaze yesterday, the government said. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney posted on X that "a serious incident creating a major fire" had occurred at Canadian Forces 'Base Wainwright' military base in western Alberta province. There were "both fatalities and injuries" as a result of the incident, the country's defence minister, David McGuinty, said at a news conference. Neither offered details on number of casualties or the nature of the incident. "We will have more to say in the coming hours and days," Mr McGuinty added. A doctor at a hospital in the city of Edmonton, about 200km (110 miles) northwest of the base, told public broadcaster CBC that Wainwright's healthcare facilities were "completely overwhelmed" by the number of patients requiring care.

stories.title: Murder probe after body of man found near river in Cork
stories.summary: Gardaí are treating as murder the death of a man whose body was found on a walkway near the River Blackwater, two kilometres from Mallow in Co Cork on Thursday. It follows the completion of a post-mortem examination by the Assistant State Pathologist, Dr Margot Bolster. Gardaí say they are not releasing the post-mortem examination results for operational reasons, but it is understood they indicate the man died violently. He has been named locally as Paul O'Connor from Ballyphehane in Cork. He was 56 years old. It is believed that Mr O'Connor travelled from Kent Train Station in Cork city to Mallow Train Station on Wednesday, arriving there after 7.20pm. Gardaí say that at the time, he was wearing a dark green hooded jacket, khaki coloured combat trousers and black runners.

stories.summary: Aontú is to table a Dáil motion of no confidence in the Minister for Foreign Affairs Helen McEntee over her handling of garda whistleblower allegations. Aontú leader Peadar Tóibín confirmed his party will use its Dáil time on 4 November to bring forward the motion which will focus on Ms McEntee's tenure as Minister for Justice between 2020 and 2025. The programme revealed that two people who handled protected disclosures made by garda whistleblowers have themselves blown the whistle, alleging that reforms introduced to protect those who speak out have been undermined by senior management. They were among four garda whistleblowers speaking publicly for the first time in the programme. The Dáil heard claims that Ms McEntee "usurped the role" of the Office of the Protected Disclosure Commission by referring to An Garda Síochana a protected disclosure made to her. The Fine Gael Meath East TD rejected the claims, insisting she adhered to the law "at all times".

stories.title: Diesel prices: can US-Russia deal ease global pressure?
stories.summary: Diesel prices have continued their upward trend during September and October, surpassing €2.10 per litre this month. According to the latest estimates from AA, the national average reached €2.14 in October, a 24% increase compared to February this year. The cost of fuel, which is crucial for logistics and farming, as well as for millions of private motorists, has soared globally. Diesel margins, or the "crack spread" - which measures how much money refineries make from selling a barrel of diesel compared with the price of crude oil - have also reached record levels. There is a cost in turning "something useless into something useful", Dr Paul Deane, Senior Lecturer at the University College Cork, explained. "That is essentially what we call crack spreads or refinery spreads. That reflects the amount of money that the refinery gets for converting oil into a useful product." Back in February, refineries earned around $32 per barrel of diesel. In September, this margin rose to $107.

stories.title: Trump's new press secretary 'let go' five days into role
stories.summary: White House Press Secretary Katie Zacharia was "let go" from the role, a White House official has said, after US President Donald Trump said he had told her to reconsider the job following public scrutiny. "I told her: 'I think you're better off being happy, and I'm not sure you can ever be happy in this stuff.' There's nothing easy about this stuff," Mr Trump told reporters while departing the White House. He added: "I said to her honestly, 'If I were you, I'd reconsider... think about it. But I would reconsider.'" Fox News, citing a White House official, later reported that Ms Zacharia was "transitioning" out of the role of press secretary. Ms Zacharia started the job on Monday and held her debut White House briefing on Tuesday. Over the last week, the issue of whether Ms Zacharia, a graduate of California's Pepperdine University law school, had actually passed the bar - making her an attorney - came under fire.

stories.title: O'Donoghue proud as Munster victorious on emotional night
stories.summary: It's never easy for Munster, and they are often an emotional team, but this week was like no other. Saturday night’s 33-25 win over Racing 92 came ten years and one day on from the sad passing of then-Munster head coach Anthony Foley, on the eve of a fixture against the same team. Few moments summed up like the poignancy of the occasion like what followed the full-time whistle, as a large group of players, coaches and staff gathered in the middle of the Cork field to sing the club’s unique anthem, "Stand Up and Fight". Double-centurion Jack O’Donoghue was a young 22-year-old when Munster did the same thing in their win over Glasgow Warriors, in Thomond Park on the day after Foley’s funeral. He is a wise 32-year-old veteran now, but the emotion remains the same for the Waterford man. "For me personally, it was very emotional", the Waterford native said. "I stood in that circle ten years ago as a young fella just coming through. "I was asked after the game what Axel meant to me and he gave me my first opportunity. He put time and effort into me and sitting down as an academy player, watching videos, watching training and teaching me the little intricate bits of the game.
